title: Carl Sagan, the astronomer who ended up arrested in the Nevada desert
excerpt: Carl Sagan was arrested twice in the Nevada desert for protesting against atomic tests. The science communicator who brought the universe closer to millions also argued that science obliges you to take a stand. Did you know?
content:
Carl Sagan, the voice that brought the universe closer to millions of people, was arrested twice in the Nevada desert for protesting against atomic tests. The topic comes from a 2011 Milenio 3 (Cadena SER) special about the scientist and the search for extraterrestrial life. On foro3d.com we review that lesser-known side of the science communicator, the one of the scientist who argued that science also obliges you to take a stand.

From Cosmos to the site line: what is known about his arrests 🔭

In the mid-1980s, concerned about the risk of nuclear war and author of the studies on nuclear winter, Sagan joined the protests against the atomic tests that the United States was still carrying out at the Nevada Test Site. In the fall of 1986 he was arrested along with more than a hundred members of the American Public Health Association. On February 5, 1987, after a rally of nearly 2,000 people, he was detained again along with more than 400 demonstrators, among them the actors Martin Sheen and Kris Kristofferson, for crossing the site line. What the Milenio 3 special presented as a curious anecdote is today a documented episode of his biography.

The man who looked at the stars and ended up in handcuffs ✨

There is a kind of gentle irony in the image: the astronomer who explained the immensity of the cosmos with an almost impossible calm ended up crossing an imaginary line in the desert and being arrested for it. The legend of the serene sage clashes with that of the activist who decided that staying silent was not an option. Did you know this side of Sagan? If you know anything more about those protests or about his stance on nuclear testing, tell us.
